text_en: Information security roles and responsibilities: security responsibilities are defined and allocated according to organisational needs
Segregation of duties: conflicting duties and areas of responsibility are separated to reduce unauthorised or unintentional modification or misuse of assets
Management responsibilities: management requires all personnel to apply information security in accordance with the established policies and procedures
Contact with authorities: the organisation establishes and maintains contact with relevant authorities
Contact with special interest groups: the organisation maintains contact with special interest groups and professional security forums
Threat intelligence: information about information security threats is collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence
Information security in project management: information security is integrated into project management
Inventory of information and other associated assets: an inventory of information and associated assets including owners is developed and maintained
Acceptable use of information and other associated assets: rules for acceptable use and handling of information and assets are identified and implemented
Return of assets: personnel and external parties return organisational assets on termination of their employment or agreement
Classification of information: information is classified according to confidentiality integrity availability and relevant requirements
Labelling of information: an appropriate set of procedures for information labelling is developed and implemented
Information transfer: rules procedures and agreements protect information transfer for all types of transfer facilities
Access control: rules to control physical and logical access to information and assets are established based on business and security requirements
Identity management: the full life cycle of identities is managed
Authentication information: allocation and management of authentication information such as passwords is controlled and users are advised to handle it properly
Access rights: access rights to information and assets are provisioned reviewed modified and removed according to policy
Information security in supplier relationships: processes and procedures manage the information security risks associated with the use of supplier products and services
Addressing information security within supplier agreements: relevant information security requirements are established and agreed with each supplier
Managing information security in the ICT supply chain: processes manage information security risks in the ICT products and services supply chain
Monitoring review and change management of supplier services: the organisation monitors reviews and manages changes to supplier information security practices and service delivery
Information security for use of cloud services: acquisition use management and exit from cloud services follow information security requirements
Information security incident management planning and preparation: the organisation plans and prepares for managing incidents by defining processes roles and responsibilities
Assessment and decision on information security events: the organisation assesses information security events and decides whether to categorise them as incidents
Response to information security incidents: information security incidents are responded to in accordance with documented procedures
Learning from information security incidents: knowledge gained from incidents is used to strengthen and improve information security controls
Collection of evidence: procedures for identification collection acquisition and preservation of evidence related to incidents are established
Information security during disruption: the organisation plans how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption
ICT readiness for business continuity: ICT readiness is planned implemented maintained and tested based on business continuity objectives
Legal statutory regulatory and contractual requirements: relevant requirements and the organisation approach to meeting them are identified documented and kept up to date
Intellectual property rights: appropriate procedures protect intellectual property rights
Protection of records: records are protected from loss destruction falsification unauthorised access and unauthorised release
Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information: the organisation identifies and meets requirements for the preservation of privacy and protection of PII
Independent review of information security: the approach to managing information security is reviewed independently at planned intervals or when significant changes occur
Compliance with policies rules and standards for information security: compliance with the organisation information security policy and standards is regularly reviewed
Documented operating procedures: operating procedures for information processing facilities are documented and made available to personnel who need them
